reviews.review_text: I really like Scottsdale Gateway. Generous amount of parking areas, timely garbage pickup, timely notification and frequent updates of unplanned problems w/ utilities (and prompt repair or work-around), the investment made in, and the upkeep of, the pool areas and the other grounds, the convenience of the laundry facilities along w/ the large number of washers and dryers, access to reasonably-priced, fast and reliable internet services - really, everything needed to live, comfortably, made Scottsdale Gateway a great and lucky choice.  Plus, it turned out that this part of Tempe has great access to work in virtually any location, especially for tech.  And, Scottsdale Gateway is affordable - there's a lot more to apartment living than just the apartment, and after thinking of all the services provided for the price, and writing them down, I think I just talked myself into renewing my lease. reviews.review_text: I leased a studio for here for 5 months while my house was under renovation. It was essentially a storage unit with a shower. When we arrived the door was unlocked and the apartment had been ransacked. All of the boxes were ripped open and disheveled. Sadly, the last of the boxes were full of things from my childhood, and some family things. Nothing of any real value, and to be honest I couldn't really tell if anything was missing. I hadn't gone thru some of them myself in years. So we decided against calling the police. I did however go down to the office to report it. After having me write down what happened, they told me that TWO of my neighbors had actually called to report hearing activity in the apartment over the weekend. Several of the office personnel knew my situation and that I wasn't living in the apartment, including the guy I was reporting to. I asked him why he didn't give me a f-ing courtesy call and he said "he didn't want to bug me". I took him back to the apartment and showed him that there were no signs of forced entry and implied that it was someone with access to a key. He was like "that's weird, because there are only 2 keys: the 1 you have, and the 1 in the office." Did I mention that the office personnel knew of my living situation? The following day, Monday, I return to do my walk-thru and turn in my keys. I sat there with my check book and ASKED if I owed anything for those few days into March. I was told NO, any remaining utilities would be deducted from my security deposit which I would receive by mail within 14 days. Fast forward about 6 weeks later, after being redirected and redirected and several unreturned voicemails, I finally got ahold of someone at their office in Seattle. According to him, BOTH my email and forwarding address were incorrect in their records. Long story short, he ended up emailing me a breakdown of where my $450 security deposit was going and that I in fact owe them $17. Among the deductions were prorated rent thru the 5th (even though they scheduled my walk-thru and took my keys on the 2nd), a $50 LATE FEE for not paying said rent on time, a cleaning fee (IF warranted, one would think should be taken out of the $200 nonrefundable deposit), the last month's utilities (fair), and "final" utilities which were 3X the cost of the monthly. We tried tirelessly to fight every line of it, ended up getting redirected to the voicemail of a supervisor up in Seattle, and now it's May and I still haven't heard back, let alone seen a penny. At this point I'm just checking my mail everyday for that bill for $17 which I imagine I'll indefinitely end up having to pay so this doesn't end up in collections and destroying my credit. Such. A. Nightmare. Stay away. They are crooks and clearly in the business of scamming deposits. I wish I would have checked Yelp beforehand, because I'm clearly not the 1st person they've done this to. Don't be the next.
